title: awk Programming: Control Flow & Functions ⚙️
description: Implement logic with if, while, for, arrays, and string/numeric functions in awk.

slides.title: awk as a Programming Language 💻
slides.content:
## Beyond Print

awk supports:
- `if (condition) statement` / `if-else`
- `while`, `for`, `do-while` loops
- Arrays (associative by default)
- Arithmetic and string functions
- User‑defined functions

This turns awk into a powerful data‑manipulation engine.

quizData.question: How do you write an if‑else in awk?
quizData.explanation: awk's syntax resembles C: `if (condition) statement else statement`, with curly braces for blocks.

slides.title: Loops in awk 🔁
slides.content:
## Process Fields or Repeat Actions

- `for (i=1; i<=NF; i++)` – iterate over fields.
- `for (key in array)` – iterate over array indices.
- `while (condition) { ... }`

Example: reverse fields:
```awk
{ for(i=NF; i>=1; i--) printf "%s ", $i; print "" }
```

slides.title: Loop Over Fields
slides.content: Print each field on its own line:
slides.codeSnippet: echo "apple banana cherry" | awk '{ for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) print "Field "i": "$i }'

quizData.question: awk arrays are numerically indexed by default.
quizData.explanation: awk arrays are associative – the index is a string; numeric indices are converted to strings.

slides.title: Associative Arrays in awk 🗃️
Word Frequency
slides.content: Count how many times each word appears:
slides.codeSnippet:
echo -e "cat
dog
cat
bird
dog
dog" | awk '{ a[$1]++ } END { for (w in a) print w, a[w] }'

slides.title: Built‑in Functions 🎨
slides.content:
## String and Math

- `length(str)`, `substr(str,pos,len)`, `index(str,sub)`
- `tolower(str)`, `toupper(str)`
- `split(str, array, sep)` – split a string into an array.
- `int(num)`, `sqrt(num)`, `rand()`
- `sprintf(format, ...)` – format output.

These make text transformation easy.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Use `awk 'BEGIN { srand(); print int(rand()*100) }'` to generate random numbers.
